brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules make up the CTFS platform?
choices: Three modules
Four modules
Five modules
Six modules
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—GrantPlan, Contracting, Forecasting, Site Payments, and Analytics make up the five-module CTFS suite.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The CTFS platform consists of five core modules, not three, four, or six. You'll want to know each one by name and function for TechIQ conversations.

questions.question: What is the primary pain point that Gilbert, the Clinical Operations Director, is trying to solve?
choices: Compliance risk and audit trail management
Site satisfaction and payment cycle delays
AI investment alignment with existing systems
Data security and integration architecture
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—Gilbert is focused on speed, site satisfaction, and reducing manual processes that slow payment cycles.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Gilbert's world is trial execution. While compliance and data security matter to other personas, Gilbert is specifically frustrated by manual financial drag that delays site activation and payment cycles.

questions.question: How much has CTFS processed in total payments?
choices: $5 billion
$15 billion
$30 billion
$55 billion
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the $15 billion in payments processed is a key proof point that anchors your pitch and demonstrates IQVIA's track record at scale.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The $15 billion figure is one of your most powerful proof points when buyers push back on adoption or ask why IQVIA. Make sure this number is in your anchor set.

questions.question: What is the recommended word count for a hallway conversation pitch at TechIQ?
choices: Under 35 words
Under 75 words
Under 150 words
Under 200 words
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—under 35 words keeps a hallway pitch sharp and gives the person a reason to keep talking, not a full data dump.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The 35-word version is for quick hallway moments where you have thirty seconds and need one clear idea. The 75-word and 150-word versions are for longer conversations.

questions.question: What does the Contracting module automatically trigger in Site Payments when a CTA is signed?
choices: Budget reconciliation reports
Payment milestones informed by contract terms
Compliance audit trails
Site activation timelines
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this automation is the core value of Contracting's integration with Site Payments, eliminating manual re-entry and reconciliation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When a CTA is signed in CTFS Contracting, the system automatically informs payment milestones in Site Payments without manual transfer. This is what makes Contracting a platform player, not a standalone tool.

questions.question: What discovery question would be most effective to open a conversation with Reena, the VP IT Clinical?
choices: How are payment delays affecting your site relationships right now?
What keeps you up at night from a compliance risk standpoint?
Where are your current AI investments stalling before they reach full ROI?
How many sites are you activating per trial on average?
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this question opens Reena's world (governance, compliance, integration risk) and lets her tell you where the real pressure is in her own words.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Each persona responds to discovery questions that focus on their specific pain. Reena is thinking about compliance and integration risk, not site relationships or payment cycles. Your question needs to match the persona's priorities.

questions.question: When a buyer says "we already have a system," what is the recommended response strategy?
choices: Immediately list CTFS features that are superior
Ask what the existing system does not unify and quantify the cost of that gap
Suggest a pilot program to prove CTFS value
Acknowledge but quickly pivot to the $15 billion in processed payments
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the gap question opens a genuine conversation and usually reveals hidden costs that a buyer hasn't quantified, which is far more persuasive than feature comparison.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Feature comparison puts you on their terms and turns the conversation into a race you don't want to run. The gap question is more powerful because it helps the buyer discover the real cost of fragmentation themselves.

questions.question: What should you record in your post-TechIQ conversation notes within 90 seconds of ending a meaningful conversation?
choices: The person's title, company size, and budget level
The persona, stated pain, qualifying signals, and agreed next step
A summary of the entire pitch you delivered
The person's contact information and their competitors
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—capturing these four elements immediately ensures you retain the specific details that make follow-up personal and effective, rather than relying on memory later.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The goal of post-conversation notes is to preserve what made each conversation unique and actionable: the persona, their specific pain in their own words, signals that this is worth pursuing, and what you both agreed to next. Generic contact information is not enough.

questions.question: Why is the timing particularly important for positioning the Contracting module at TechIQ?
choices: It has been in market for over a year with extensive case studies
It reaches general availability at the end of November and will be featured prominently
Competitors have already launched similar products
Early adopters have already moved to competing platforms
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—because Contracting is brand new and reaching GA just as TechIQ happens, buyers will expect you to know it and it will be a hot topic throughout the event.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The timing of Contracting's GA at the end of November means it will be front and center at TechIQ. This is not a mature, proven module yet—it's emerging, which is exactly why early adopter positioning matters.

questions.question: How does CTFS's unification strategy differ fundamentally from the competitive positioning of point solutions?
choices: CTFS offers more features than point solutions in each category
CTFS solves the whole financial lifecycle and eliminates data handoff friction, whereas point solutions create new integration problems on either side of their single function
CTFS is less expensive than point solutions
CTFS is easier to implement than point solutions
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this is your core competitive story: the gap between disconnected point solutions creates friction and manual work, which unified architecture eliminates.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Never lead with feature comparison against point solutions. The real win is the unification story—point solutions solve one problem well but leave you needing something to connect budgets to contracts to payments. CTFS solves all three and makes the handoffs automatic.
